title: LEGION-186: hold a resumed root to the same-agent rule in the wired daemon; make the worker shim refuse a providers key that shadows a pod variable
spec: dispatch://LEGION-186 (spec, decisions made); parent review dispatch://LEGION-31/artifact/review-legion-31-parent-md findings 1 and 2
baseline: main 8fce288ef3273c99267b89c90f4faedef63a23a3 (every line number below is at this commit; the workspace @ is empty on top of it)
goal: One pull request, tier T2, branch legion/LEGION-186 off main, against main. (A) index.ts forwards every boot-token mint argument so /process/started runs the same-agent check for a resumed root; (B) a full-daemon regression test through startDaemon that fails on main (200) and passes after (409); (C) the worker shim refuses to start when a providers-Secret key is already a variable of its own environment, naming the key and its file path, before any dial or spawn; (D) three shim unit tests through the CLI's own entry with a fake spawn dependency; (E) docs/kubernetes.md's providers-Secret section, the root AGENTS.md shim line, and the daemon AGENTS.md shim bullet state the collision rule.

tasks.name: Worker shim: refuse a providers key that shadows a variable of the shim's own environment, at the CLI's entry, before any dial or spawn
designDecisions: The check lives in `readProviderEnvDir`, because that is the one place the key's FILE PATH is known (the spec requires the message to name key and path; by `cmdWorkerShimConnect` the export is a bare NAME→value map).

Order inside the loop: the existing `NAME_FILE` pointer skip FIRST, then the collision refusal. A file-pointed key is never exported, so there is nothing to shadow; refusing it would break the production pod, whose runtime sets DISPATCH_TOKEN_FILE and ENVOY_TOKEN_FILE. Pinned by one extra expect in the existing skip test.

`shimEnv[name] !== undefined` is the collision test (the same test the pointer skip uses): an EMPTY variable still shadows — the pod deliberately sets GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_HOST to "" (docs/kubernetes.md:470), and a providers key named GH_TOKEN would otherwise re-fill them.

To make the fake-spawn assertion meaningful, the CLI's worker-shim body (cli/index.ts:831-847: resolve, then build deps, then run the mode) moves into an exported `runWorkerShim(flags, argv, deps)` in worker-shim.ts and the citty `run` becomes one call. The refusal is thrown by resolution, before `deps.connect` or `deps.spawn` can run; the test proves that ordering at the entry the pod actually executes. `defaultWorkerShimDeps()` has no construction-time side effects (every effect is inside a returned closure), so building deps before resolving is safe.

`defaultWorkerShimDeps.spawn`'s `env: { ...process.env, ...env }` (worker-shim.ts:668) stays as it is: once no colliding key can reach `env`, the merge is exactly the intended export, and the existing test at worker-shim.test.ts:664-696 already proves a real spawn receives it.

steps.step: 1. docs/kubernetes.md — replace the sentence at :493-496 beginning 'Nothing else belongs in it' with
steps.text: Nothing else belongs in it — every worker pod mounts the volume and the shim exports each file that has no `<NAME>_FILE` pointer in the pod into the OMP child's environment, so a GitHub App private key here would reach every worker; the in-cluster daemon keeps those in its own daemon-only Secret (below). And a key must not be named like a variable the pod already carries — `OMP_SESSION_STORAGE`, `OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE`, any `LEGION_*`, `DISPATCH_URL`, the deliberately empty `GH_TOKEN`: that export lands over the pod's own environment, so such a key would replace the daemon's value without anything saying so (a stale `OMP_SESSION_STORAGE=file` would quietly move a Postgres deployment back to files). The shim refuses to start instead, before Oh My Pi is spawned, with a message naming the key and its file (`legion worker-shim: --provider-env-dir key OMP_SESSION_STORAGE (/var/run/legion/providers/OMP_SESSION_STORAGE) is already a variable of this pod's environment; …`); the pod is `Failed` and the daemon counts the launch failure as it does any other. A key the pod reads through a `<NAME>_FILE` pointer (`DISPATCH_TOKEN`, `ENVOY_TOKEN`) is skipped, not refused.

steps.step: 2. Root AGENTS.md:59 — inside the parenthetical, after 'e.g. DISPATCH_TOKEN', add
steps.text: ; and refusing to start — exit 1 naming the key and its file, Oh My Pi never spawned — when a key's name is already a variable of the shim's own environment, since the export would override it silently (LEGION-186)

steps.step: 3. packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md:84 — replace 'The two flags are mutually exclusive; an unreadable or blank token file is a CLI error before anything is spawned.' with
steps.text: The two flags are mutually exclusive; an unreadable or blank token file is a CLI error before anything is spawned, and so is a `--provider-env-dir` key whose name is already a variable of the shim's own environment (`readProviderEnvDir`, `cli/worker-shim.ts`): the export lands over the pod's environment, so such a key would replace a daemon-set value — `OMP_SESSION_STORAGE` first among them — without a trace; the shim exits 1 naming the key and its file, before any dial or spawn, and a key the pod reads through a `NAME_FILE` pointer is skipped as before (LEGION-186).

decisionsRecorded: Handoff phase name: the CLI and schema call this phase `plan` (`HANDOFF_PHASES` in packages/contracts/src/handoff-schema.ts), so the planner wrote `legion handoff write --phase plan`; `--phase planner` would be refused by assertPhase.

The daemon AGENTS.md carries no sentence about the provider export; the sentence the spec points at is the root AGENTS.md's Commands line (:59). Both files are edited so the spec's 'says the same' holds wherever a reader looks; nothing else in either file changes.
The collision refusal covers every variable of the shim's environment, not the two OMP_SESSION_* names (spec 'New since we talked' and 'Rejected'); an empty variable counts as set.

runWorkerShim is introduced (a ~15-line move of the citty body) so the fake-spawn assertion the spec asks for is a real ordering check at the entry the pod runs, not a tautology against a pure function; cmdWorkerShim/cmdWorkerShimConnect/resolveWorkerShimTarget stay exported and their tests untouched.

The regression test for Acceptance 1 asserts the claim object, the locator, and the info log line; it does not read persisted state (saveState is a no-op in the harness) because the route mutates the shared `state` object in place, which is what the daemon serves.

Kept index.ts's mintControllerCapability and revokeSessionCapability wrappers as they are: neither has an optional trailing parameter to lose; rewriting them would widen the diff without closing anything.
